inputs.original_text: As a parent of three children in the city’s public schools, I want to publicly apologize to the educators and staff of South Portland School District. It is beyond maddening that our district is facing another large budget shortfall requiring cutting more than 70 positions from schools. As a taxpayer, it feels that there has [...]
inputs.modified_text: A parent with three children in the public schools is apologizing to the educators and staff at South Portland School District over yet another large budget shortfall that's forcing the loss of more than 70 positions. They feel the sting as a taxpayer but blame it on long-standing structural inequalities that supposedly starve education while shielding the wealthy. That's the usual excuse from those pushing progressive ideas. In reality these repeated shortfalls are the predictable result of mismanagement inside the system itself, where priorities have drifted away from basics and toward failed experiments that erode discipline and accountability. The cuts hit families hard, but demanding more institutional reform for labor rights and equitable funding will only repeat the cycle. What we need instead is a return to personal responsibility, local control, and traditional standards that put real education and cultural continuity first.
